subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi carried a locket always, never took it off, and kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, living inside a haze on purpose.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library, carried it always, never took it off, kept his chamber thick with it, medicated his failing lungs with the smell of it, lived inside a haze on purpose

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti had been at Janussi's throat for years, drank excessively, shouted at Janussi twice in one day, called him 'nothing but a glorified book peddler,' and fled the second argument in terror.
source_quote: Daral Yashenti... those two have been at each other's throats for years... he drinks way too much... 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper'... 'nothing but a glorified book peddler'... he ran away so fast

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling Curator of the Infernal Fortress, screamed at Janussi calling him a traitor, was seen glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. carrying a lantern she had no use for, and had incurred his wrath that morning.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas... gave me the heebie-jeebies... screamed that Janussi was a traitor... glowing red in the candlelight... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library has two keys — one held by Janussi, missing from his neck, and one held by the gate warden Kalan.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan

subject: the locket
fact: The locket was missing from Janussi’s neck — he carried it always, never took it off, and it was the only thing gone from the room.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck. And that knocked something loose in his memory... Janussi carried it always, never took it off

subject: the black residue
fact: Black residue was on the man’s mouth and fingers — definitively not from the blue ink, and came from somewhere the blue ink did not.
source_quote: The black on the man's mouth came from somewhere the blue ink did not... Black. Definitively not the blue ink — Grygum had already settled that, checked it twice and certain

subject: the gift tag
fact: The gift tag read: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.' Written in a cramped, sour hand, by someone who resented the act of writing it.
source_quote: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'... cramped, sour hand... script of someone who resented the act of writing it

subject: the comedy book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was annotated with jokes and obscure spell notes in the same hand and fresh ink, then vanished from the room, leaving only its absence as proof it had been there.
source_quote: *The Golden Ass* was a comedy... writing down jokes he found funny... blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?... the same hand, the same fresh ink... the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold

subject: the murder chamber
fact: The murder chamber was filled with tobacco smoke — a habit Janussi kept to mask his failing lungs — and now served as the site where the smell of poison was hidden.
source_quote: A man who fills his own room with smoke as a habit... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: the midnight thud
fact: At midnight, Hollypocket heard a thud from above — the last sound she associated with Janussi being alive — and later recalled seeing Sylvira Savikas’s glowing red face in candlelight, carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: I heard a thud upstairs... I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight... she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: the argument with Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting around the ninth bell, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: the argument with Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch passed Hollypocket on the steps with a face like thunder, nearly knocking the tea tray out of her hands.
source_quote: I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: the confrontation with Daral at half past ten
fact: Daral Yashenti returned drunk at half past ten, pounded on Janussi’s door until let in, argued loudly, then fled down the stairs in terror — the fastest Janussi had ever seen him run.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in... another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs... I'd never seen him run away so fast

subject: the gift delivery
fact: A gift was delivered to Janussi — a Dead Winter gift inscribed by a rival — written in a resentful, cramped hand, and left in the wastebasket.
source_quote: A gift tag surfaced from the wastebasket... 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris, the assistant, identified Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-time rival and revealed that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris... 'Oh, that'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.'... 'Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.'

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, witnessed all major confrontations with Janussi, heard the midnight thud, and saw Sylvira Savikas glowing red in candlelight carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: Hollypocket... brought the keeper his morning tea... heard Teles shout 'hypocrite'... overheard Daral calling him 'glorified book peddler'... heard the midnight thud... saw Sylvira Savikas’s face glowing red... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, the Stonespeaker, used his crystal to prepare to interrogate the housecat — the only living witness in the chamber — and was the first to notice the significance of Sylvira’s lantern.
source_quote: Daz... 'I think I can talk to the cat.'... 'Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.'... Daz was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever... 'That explains the candle.'

subject: the Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow had a saying about absence — that a room tells you most by what it is missing — possibly echoed by Brother Tharusk, the tall one who always smelled of incense.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: the poison hypothesis
fact: The poison hypothesis emerged from the absence of the book, the black residue, the smoke, and the locket — all pointing to a murder masked by environmental concealment.
source_quote: The black on the pages of a book that was no longer in the room. The smoke that hid the smell of it... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: the cipher hypothesis
fact: The cipher hypothesis arose from the annotated comedy book — jokes and spell notes in the same hand, suggesting the book itself was a key to a replacement cipher.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher. Some sort of replacement cipher, and there's, like, some sort of code that the book ends up being the key to.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the gate warden, holds the second key to the Hightower Library and was seen with a face like thunder the morning of the murder.
source_quote: the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan... He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was the one who noted the significance of Sylvira’s lantern and the connection between the candlelight and the poison’s concealment.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum insisted on interviewing the housekeeper to determine what was missing — grounding the investigation in physical absence rather than political motive.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing... go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin connected the gift tag to the rivalry theory and identified the black residue as inconsistent with the blue ink, reinforcing the poison hypothesis.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing... Black. Definitively not the blue ink

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the significance of the lantern carried by Sylvira Savikas — a tiefling who needs no light — and was the first to link it to the candlelight as a cover for poison.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep’s culture — not the library, but the scholars — is defined by grudges filed like scrolls, polished over years, and deployed as weapons.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold, sitting on them for years, polishing them

subject: the discovery of the missing book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was confirmed missing from the room, its absence the only physical change, and its annotations the only evidence of its presence.
source_quote: the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold... And now it was gone, and it was the only thing gone

subject: the final hypothesis
fact: The final hypothesis combined poison, cipher, and rivalry — the book was a cipher key, the smoke concealed poison, the locket was stolen to implicate a rival, and Daral and Sylvira were the prime suspects.
source_quote: The poison and the cipher could both be true. The missing book carried both. We had read the room down to what it was willing to give. The rest of it lived somewhere else, and we'd have to go find it.
